question: Can a second frozen encoder improve a trained model by contributing information that cannot be reconstructed from the first encoder?
new_mechanism: Compare feature-level fusion with the previously studied probability averaging. The established linear GTE reference retains all lexical and corpus features. On unique fitting texts, learn an unlabeled ridge map from standardized GTE sentence vectors to the second encoder's standardized vectors. Use the 32 highest-variance axes of the unexplained residual as extra signed pair features. Fit one logistic head jointly, with the same regularization and side swap as the reference. Test the second view from a sentence-similarity model (MiniLM-L12) and from a replaced-token detector (ELECTRA).
selection: Compare both new feature-level fusions alone and equally blended with the frozen GTE on the primary partition. Lock the best two distinct choices, confirm on the second fold, and use the identical eligibility, worst-fold tie breaker and third-fold rules of protocol.json. Maximum five new supervised fits. The ridge projection and PCA never see labels. A winning research combination does not become an autonomous course result without a new cold run.
data: Only official training rows, no designated validation or formal test. Exact public model revisions and label-free sentence caches may be reused.
